title: kate-core: choose a newline from the indenter name
summary: newline_for_indenter picks python_newline or newline_insertion from the indenter name. The newline command still calls newline_insertion. Linux CI runs the test.

lane.reason: The work is pure Rust in kate-core. Linux CI runs the test. The newline command stays on newline_insertion.

definitions.definition:
#[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]
pub fn newline_for_indenter(
    indenter: Option<&str>,
    buf: &kate_text::TextBuffer,
    at: kate_text::Offset,
    config: &crate::DocumentConfig,
) -> String

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: None and any name other than python or cstyle call newline_insertion with cstyle false. cstyle calls newline_insertion with cstyle true. python calls python_newline. The function has cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code)). Leave workspace.rs unchanged. The existing newline tests stay green. Leave theme.rs, paint.rs, layout.rs, and session.rs unchanged. PKT-0085, PKT-0088, and PKT-0089 own those files. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip.

regression_tests.name: indent::tests::newline_for_indenter_picks_python
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main because newline_for_indenter does not exist. For def f(): at the end of the line, the python indenter returns a newline plus four spaces. The cstyle indenter on four spaces, foo, brace returns a newline plus eight spaces. A missing indenter on foo returns a newline.
